stem: A solutions architect must replace a homegrown script that polls two Regions and manually updates DNS records during a failover. Which purpose-built service replaces it?

choices.text: A scheduled Lambda function that checks both endpoints and updates the Route 53 records through the API.
CloudWatch alarms that page an on-call engineer when the primary endpoint's health check fails.
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery, failing traffic over between the two Regions.
Amazon Route 53 with a failover routing policy backed by health checks.

rationale: Route 53 failover routing, paired with health checks, is the purpose-built managed feature that already monitors an endpoint and stops returning it in DNS answers once it is unhealthy, replacing the homegrown polling-and-update script entirely. A scheduled Lambda function that polls endpoints and updates records through the API is still custom-built tooling doing the same job as the homegrown script, not the purpose-built managed alternative. CloudWatch alarms that page an on-call engineer still rely on a human to make the DNS change, rather than replacing that manual step with an automated one. AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery fails over replicated servers between Regions; it does not perform DNS-level traffic routing, so it does not replace this particular script.
